description: Walking with correct posture at varying paces
instructions: Walk with correct posture. Brisk power walk in first trimester, slightly slower stroll in 3rd trimester.
benefits: Excellent cardiovascular exercise suitable for all fitness levels
notes: Adjust pace as pregnancy progresses. Maintain proper posture throughout.

instructions: Swim at comfortable pace using proper form. Water provides support to joints.
benefits: Strengthens back, arm, and leg muscles. Water supports joints. Excellent cardiovascular exercise.
notes: Water provides natural support to growing body

instructions: Cycle at moderate pace on stationary bike. Adjust resistance as needed.
benefits: Low risk of falling. Safe cardiovascular option.
notes: Significantly lower risk of falling than outdoor bicycling
safety_considerations: Safe during pregnancy - lower fall risk than outdoor cycling

instructions: Use elliptical or arc trainer at comfortable pace and resistance.
benefits: Lower impact on joints than running
notes: Regarded as secure forms of cardio

instructions: Follow low-impact prenatal aerobics program. Many available digitally online.
benefits: Structured cardio routine designed for pregnancy
notes: Many digital fitness classes available online
safety_considerations: Choose low-impact programs designed for pregnancy

instructions: Perform standard push-ups or knee push-ups with proper form.
notes: Only if doing them regularly pre-pregnancy
safety_considerations: First trimester only if previously performed regularly

instructions:
1. Face a wall, place hands on wall just outside shoulder-width apart.
2. Contract abs and hold hips in straight line with head, shoulders, and ankles.
3. Slowly bend elbows to lower chest towards wall.
4. Stop when elbows reach 90-degree angle.
5. Reverse motion to starting position.
6. Repeat.
benefits: Upper body strength with less core and back strain
notes: Regression from standard push-ups to reduce strain

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart or slightly wider for growing belly.
2. With hips in neutral position, bend knees and lower body as if sitting in chair.
3. Descend until thighs are parallel to floor, keeping core engaged, pulling belly button toward spine.
4. Push through heels to stand back to starting position.
5. Can use chair/bench for support initially.
benefits: Strengthens legs, glutes, core, and pelvic floor muscles - essential during childbirth
notes: Adjust stance width for comfort as belly grows

instructions: Continue barbell/weighted squats with proper form if performed pre-pregnancy.
safety_considerations: Generally safe to continue in first trimester if done pre-pregnancy

instructions: Continue weightlifting with modifications: reduce weight used, omit exercises on back, listen to body.
notes: Modify as body changes. Reduce weight. Omit any exercises performed on back.
safety_considerations: Safe to continue if done pre-pregnancy. Must modify and reduce weight.
exercises_to_avoid: Any exercises performed lying on back after 1st trimester

description: Bicep curls while sitting on stability ball
instructions:
1. Sit on stability ball with feet firmly planted shoulder-width apart.
2. Sit up tall with neutral hips, head over chest, chest over hips.
3. Engage core by pulling belly button toward spine.
4. With dumbbell in each hand, palms facing up.
5. Slowly bring hand toward shoulder, bending at elbow.
6. Pause at top and return to starting position.
7. Repeat with other hand.
benefits: Increases arm strength while engaging core and back muscles for stability
notes: Stability ball provides support while engaging core

description: Tricep extensions while sitting on stability ball
instructions:
1. Sit on stability ball with feet firmly planted shoulder-width apart.
2. Sit up tall with neutral hips, head over chest, chest over hips.
3. Engage core by pulling belly button toward spine.
4. With light weight in one hand, raise hand above head in neutral position.
5. Bending only at elbow, lower hand toward back, extending tricep.
6. Slowly return to starting position.
notes: Use light weight. Ball stabilization engages core.

instructions:
1. Sit on stability ball with feet firmly planted on floor.
2. Sit with hips in neutral position.
3. While exhaling, slowly curl hips forward, rounding lower back.
4. Initiate movement from core, not legs.
5. Inhale and return to starting position.
benefits: Develops deep core muscles. Helps relieve back pain.
notes: Focus on core initiation, not leg movement

instructions:
1. Sit on stability ball with feet firmly planted shoulder-width apart.
2. Sit up tall with neutral hips, head over chest, chest over hips.
3. Engage core by pulling belly button toward spine.
4. While slowly exhaling, lift one foot off ground.
5. Lower foot while exhaling.
6. Repeat with other foot.
benefits: Core stability and balance. Helps relieve back pain.
notes: Maintain balance and control throughout movement

instructions: Hold standard plank position with proper form.
Perform plank with hands elevated on bench. Hold for short intervals of 5-10 seconds at a time.
benefits: Core strength with reduced abdominal strain
notes: Stop immediately if you feel strain, bulging, or discomfort in abdominal muscles
safety_considerations: Modified version to lessen abdominal strain. Stop if any discomfort.

description: Prenatal yoga, hatha yoga, or restorative yoga
instructions: Participate in prenatal yoga, hatha yoga, or restorative yoga classes. Speak to instructor about modifications. Pay attention to how you feel.
notes: Inform instructor you are pregnant. Best types: prenatal yoga, hatha yoga, restorative yoga.
safety_considerations: Avoid inversions, big bends, and positions on back. Stop or modify if feeling strain.
exercises_to_avoid: Hot yoga (not safe), inversions, big bends, any positions on back
